title: Madlab - The Ultimate Innovation Hackathon
description: MADLAB — Crazy Ideas. Real Execution. A Multidisciplinary Innovation Hackathon About the Opportunity MADLAB is a high-energy, multidisciplinary hackathon designed for individuals who dare to think differently, communicate confidently, build creatively, and execute ideas into practical solutions. The competition brings together software developers, marketing enthusiasts, sales strategists, business students, designers, and aspiring entrepreneurs to solve challenges through innovation, teamwork, and strategic thinking. This is not just a coding competition. Participants will be evaluated on their creativity, technical and practical skills, communication, problem-solving, marketing strategies, sales approach, and ability to present and execute ideas. Eligibility Criteria Open to college students and aspiring professionals with an interest in technology, business, marketing, sales, design, or entrepreneurship. Participants from all academic streams and specializations are welcome. Students from different colleges can form a team together (inter-college participation is allowed). Participants from different specializations can collaborate in the same team (inter-specialization participation is encouraged). No advanced coding experience is mandatory. Creativity, communication, business thinking, and execution matter just as much as technical skills. Participants must provide accurate registration details and follow the event organizers' instructions. Team Formation Participants may register individually or in teams of 2–5 members. Teams may include developers, marketers, sales representatives, designers, presenters, and business strategists. Each team should distribute responsibilities effectively and ensure that every member contributes. Each team must nominate one member as its primary point of contact. Team changes after registration require approval from the organizers. Competition Format and Rounds Round 1: The Spark — Problem-Solving and Ideation (30 minutes) Teams receive a problem statement and identify the problem, target audience, and potential solution. They must demonstrate original thinking, practical reasoning, and a clear understanding of the challenge. Round 2: The Build Lab — Creation and Strategy (90 minutes) Teams develop a working prototype, business concept, marketing campaign, sales strategy, or another relevant solution according to the assigned challenge. Developers can build prototypes, marketers can design campaigns, and sales-oriented participants can develop pitches and customer acquisition strategies. Round 3: The Pitch Arena — Presentation and Communication (5–7 minutes per team) Each team presents its solution to the judges, explaining the problem, proposed solution, target audience, implementation strategy, and expected impact. Teams must communicate their ideas clearly and confidently. Round 4: The Crossfire — Judges' Q&A (3–5 minutes per team) Judges question teams about their decisions, originality, feasibility, technical implementation, marketing approach, sales strategy, and scalability. Participants must demonstrate ownership of their work and respond professionally. Total estimated competition duration: 2.5–4 hours, depending on the number of teams and event scheduling. Problem Statements Participants will receive one assigned problem statement or challenge from the organizers. Challenges may cover the following areas: Technology and Development: Build a prototype, tool, website, application, or automation that solves a real-world problem. Marketing and Creativity: Develop a creative marketing campaign, brand strategy, social media concept, or customer engagement plan. Sales and Business Growth: Create a sales pitch, customer acquisition strategy, conversion plan, or business growth model. Communication and Innovation: Present an original idea, demonstrate persuasive communication, and turn a concept into an actionable solution. The final problem statement, required deliverables, and evaluation criteria will be communicated to participants before the relevant round begins. Evaluation Criteria Participants will be evaluated on the following criteria: Creativity and originality — 20% Problem-solving and practical execution — 20% Technical or domain-specific skills — 20% Communication and presentation — 15% Marketing, sales, and business thinking — 15% Teamwork, adaptability, and Q&A performance — 10% Judges' decisions will be final, subject to the event's published rules. Competition Rules All submissions must be created or substantially developed by the participating team during the competition, unless the organizers explicitly permit pre-existing resources. Pre-existing code, templates, AI tools, and third-party resources may be used only as permitted by the organizers. Teams must disclose significant external contributions. Plagiarism, copied submissions presented as original work, fabricated results, impersonation, and misrepresentation of contributions are prohibited. Every team member must contribute meaningfully to the competition. Participants must respect fellow competitors, judges, mentors, volunteers, and organizers. Teams must submit their deliverables before the announced deadline. Late submissions may be penalized or disqualified. Participants must not attempt unauthorized access to systems, misuse personal data, or engage in unethical or illegal activities. All presentations must be professional, relevant to the assigned challenge, and completed within the allocated time. Participants must follow the venue's safety requirements and the organizers' instructions throughout the event. Any disputes, rule violations, or exceptional circumstances will be reviewed by the organizing committee. Deliverables Each team must submit the relevant deliverables for its assigned challenge, which may include: A working prototype, demonstration, campaign concept, sales pitch, or business solution. A short explanation of the problem and the proposed solution. A presentation outlining the approach, target audience, execution plan, and expected impact. Supporting materials such as designs, mock-ups, code, campaign creatives, or a business model, where applicable. Final Note MADLAB is an opportunity to move beyond ideas and demonstrate what you can create, communicate, build, market, and sell. Whether you are a developer, marketer, salesperson, designer, or business thinker, your skills have a place in the lab. Bring your creativity. Challenge the ordinary. Execute the extraordinary. MADLAB — Crazy Ideas. Real Execution. Note: The organizers should confirm the final team size, eligibility, round timings, problem statements, judging panel, submission process, and prizes before publishing the opportunity. Any details not yet finalized should be updated to reflect the actual event rules.

title: Codegeist 2026: Build with context. Ship with confidence.
Tatusta
description: Overview Innovate. Build. Break Barriers. About the Hackathon ISTE TCET invites passionate innovators, developers, designers, and problem-solvers to participate in an exciting hackathon that challenges participants to transform ideas into impactful solutions. The hackathon provides a platform for students to collaborate, think creatively, explore emerging technologies, and develop innovative solutions to real-world problems. Whether you are a coder, designer, researcher, or aspiring entrepreneur, this is your opportunity to showcase your skills, experiment with technology, and bring your ideas to life. Work in teams, tackle challenging problem statements, build functional prototypes, and compete with fellow innovators. Push your limits, learn from the experience, and turn your imagination into innovation! Domains Participants can explore innovative solutions across the following domains: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning (AI/ML): Intelligent systems, predictive analytics, automation, generative AI, and AI-powered applications. Web Development: Innovative websites, web applications, SaaS platforms, and digital solutions. Mobile Application Development: Android/iOS applications, cross-platform solutions, and mobile-first innovations. Blockchain & Web3: Decentralized applications, smart contracts, digital identity, and secure transactions. Cybersecurity: Network security, threat detection, data privacy, and secure digital infrastructure. Internet of Things (IoT): Smart devices, automation, connected systems, and sensor-based solutions. Healthcare & MedTech: Healthcare accessibility, patient management, medical innovation, and wellness solutions. FinTech: Digital payments, financial inclusion, banking solutions, and financial automation. Sustainability & Smart Cities: Environmental solutions, waste management, energy efficiency, and smart infrastructure. Open Innovation: Any technology-driven solution addressing a meaningful real-world problem. Participation Guidelines Participation is open to eligible college students. Participants must register within the specified registration deadline. Teams may consist of 2–4 members . Interdisciplinary teams are encouraged. Each team must nominate one team leader as the primary point of contact. All team members must be registered successfully. Hackathon Rules & Regulations All projects must be developed during the designated hackathon period. Pre-existing projects cannot be submitted as original hackathon solutions. However, previously developed libraries, frameworks, and open-source tools may be used. Teams must develop solutions relevant to the selected domain or assigned problem statement. Plagiarism, duplication, and misrepresentation of work will result in disqualification. Teams must submit their source code, project documentation, and working prototype within the stipulated deadline. Participants must ensure that their projects are functional and demonstrable during evaluation. Any use of AI tools, APIs, third-party libraries, and open-source resources must be appropriately acknowledged. Teams must maintain professional conduct throughout the event. The decision of the judging panel and organizing committee will be final. Organizers reserve the right to modify the event schedule, rules, or guidelines when necessary. Evaluation Criteria Projects will be evaluated based on the following parameters: Innovation & Originality: 20% Technical Implementation: 25% Problem Relevance & Impact: 20% Functionality & Execution: 20% Presentation & Pitch: 15% Project Submission Requirements Each team must submit: Project title and selected domain. Problem statement and proposed solution. Working prototype or Minimum Viable Product (MVP). Source code repository (GitHub or equivalent). Project presentation (PPT). Brief documentation explaining the implementation, technology stack, and future scope. Demonstration of the working solution. What to Expect An opportunity to transform ideas into real-world solutions. Hands-on experience with emerging technologies. Networking and collaboration with fellow innovators. Expert evaluation and feedback. Recognition, certificates, and exciting prizes for outstanding teams. Important Note Participants are expected to bring their own laptops and any additional hardware required for their projects. Further information regarding the venue, schedule, problem statements, submission deadlines, and other event-specific instructions will be communicated by the organizing committee. Organized by ISTE TCET Think Beyond. Build Beyond. Innovate Beyond.

title: ELUCode - 7
description: Overview: ELUCode is a fast-paced 2-hour competitive coding contest by EduLinkUp designed to challenge your problem-solving ability, algorithmic thinking, and coding speed. The contest brings together students and developers from across the community to compete on a set of carefully curated problems ranging from logical puzzles to algorithmic challenges. Participants will face multiple problems of varying difficulty levels, testing their understanding of data structures, algorithms, logic building, and efficient coding practices. Whether you are a beginner exploring competitive programming or an experienced coder looking to sharpen your skills, ELUCode provides a platform to learn, compete, and showcase your abilities. Top performers will be recognised through special achievement badges and certificates within the EduLinkUp ecosystem. Scoring: Each challenge carries a predefined score, based on its difficulty level. A participant’s score for a challenge depends on the number of test cases successfully passed by their submission. Submissions are automatically evaluated against hidden and visible test cases to ensure correctness and efficiency. The overall leaderboard is determined by the total score obtained across all challenges. If two or more participants achieve the same score, the tie will be broken based on the sum of time of the first correct solution for all the problems. The participant who reaches the score earlier will rank higher.

title: Technova 2027
description: Technova 2027 – Startup-First Hackathon Think. Build. Innovate. Pitch. Technova 2027 is an 8-hour startup-first hackathon organized by Burhani College, Mumbai. It is designed to bring together creative thinkers, developers, innovators, and aspiring entrepreneurs to solve real-world problems through technology. Unlike traditional hackathons, TECHNOVA focuses not only on building applications but also on developing practical solutions with business potential. Participants will be challenged to think like startup founders, build a functional Minimum Viable Product (MVP), and present their ideas effectively. Event Details: Event: Technova 2027 Date: January 2027 Duration: 8 Hours Venue: Burhani College, 10 Nesbit Road, Mazgaon, Mumbai, Maharashtra – 400010 Team Size: 2–4 Participants Format: Startup-First Hackathon Eligibility & Team Rules: Each Team Must Have a Minimum of 2 and A Maximum of 4 Participants. Solo Participation Is Not Allowed. Cross-College Teams Are Allowed and Encouraged. Each Participant Can Be Part of Only One Team. Teams Must Be Finalized Before the Event. Team Switching During the Hackathon Is Not Permitted. Team Members Cannot Be Changed Later than 2 Days Before the Event. Every Participant Must Carry a valid government-issued ID proof and college ID card. Registration & Selection Process: Registration Will Be Conducted Through the Official Unstop Opportunity. Participants Must Provide Accurate Details of All Team Members. Linked in Profile Links Must Be Submitted as Part of The Registration Process. Participation Is Subject to Limited Slots. If Registrations Exceed the Available Capacity, Teams Will Be Shortlisted Based on Their Linked in Presence and Submitted Profiles. Selection Will Follow a First-Come, First-Served Approach, Subject to Linked In-Based Shortlisting and Available Slots. Registration Does Not Guarantee Selection. Only Approved and Confirmed Teams Will Be Eligible to Participate. Hackathon Format – Color-Based Challenge System: Technova Introduces a Unique Color-Based Problem Allocation System. Participants Select One of Five Available Colors. Each Team Receives a Corresponding Colored Wristband During Registration at The Venue. A Problem Set Will Be Assigned Based on The Selected Color and Revealed Later. Each Team Must Choose One Problem Statement from Its Assigned Set. Teams Work on Developing an Mvp and Preparing Their Final Pitch. This System Promotes Fairness, Creativity, and Equal Opportunities for All Teams. Challenge Tracks: Participants Will Work on Problem Statements from One of The Following Five Tracks: Digital Trust: verify Before You Believe Money & Markets: make Finance Work for Everyone From Soil to Shelf: rethink the Food Chain Technology without Barriers: build for Every Ability Ai that Gets Things Done: move Beyond Chatbots ️ Build Rules: All Project Development Must Take Place During the Hackathon. Pre-Built Projects Are Strictly Prohibited. Open-Source Tools and Ai Tools Are Allowed. Plagiarism and Copying Are Not Permitted. Teams Must Develop Their Solutions According to Their Selected Problem Statement. Participants Must Maintain Professional and Respectful Conduct. Submission Requirements: Every Team Must Submit: Git Hub Repository: complete Project Source Code. Pitch Deck (ppt): explanation of The Problem, Solution, Business Model, and Project Value. Demo / Prototype: a Working Demonstration of The Developed Solution. Note: submission Deadlines and Formats Are Strict. No Extensions or Exceptions Will Be Provided. Judging Criteria: Projects Will Be Evaluated on The Following Parameters: MVP Quality – Does the Solution Actually Work? Innovation & Creativity – Is the Idea Fresh and Innovative? Technical Execution – Is the Solution Functional, Clean, and Scalable? Problem Clarity – Does It Solve a Real-World Problem? Market Feasibility – Would People Actually Use It? Revenue Potential – Can It Become a Sustainable Business? Presentation & Pitch – how Effectively Is the Idea Communicated?
